<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
Path handling in the code itself needs cross-platform fixes too. Otherwise documentation claiming Windows support would be inaccurate.

A concrete plan is taking shape. It covers package.json scripts, runtime path normalization, CLI guards, coverage thresholds, hardcoded paths, documentation, and editor settings. Unix-specific commands like `rm` will be replaced with Bun-native alternatives. Documentation will switch from bash to shell blocks and note Bun shell usage. Editorconfig and gitattributes will standardize line endings.

The `AGENT=1` prefix in package.json will be removed. The environment variable will instead be injected directly inside the TypeScript coverage script, avoiding shell-specific syntax.

A `toPosixPath` helper will normalize backslashes to forward slashes before passing paths to minimatch and other utilities. Output paths will also be normalized for consistent JSON and display output.

The CLI entry guard will use Bun's `import.meta.main` property, which is the most portable way to detect whether the script is being run directly.

Minimatch requires POSIX-style paths before matching on Windows. Config exclude patterns already use forward slashes and are cross-platform. Code fixes are needed because the project already fails on Windows. Documentation and configuration will be updated alongside the code.

Active documentation such as the README and AGENTS files will be updated. Historical post-mortems may remain largely unchanged as archival material.

</details></think>

	"plan": "# Cross-platform (Windows) configuration and instructions\n\n## Findings\n\nDocs are lightly bash-labeled; the real Windows breaks are in scripts and path handling. Runtime is Bun — `bun run` provides a POSIX-like shell, but several places still assume `/` separators or Unix env syntax outside that shell.\n\n```mermaid\nflowchart LR\n  glob[\"fs.glob / Bun.Glob\"] --\u003e paths[\"paths with \\\\ on Windows\"]\n  paths --\u003e split[\"split('/')\"]\n  paths --\u003e mm[\"minimatch(relPath)\"]\n  paths --\u003e cov[\"coverage regex src/\"]\n  split --\u003e fail1[\"isSelfPath / all-rules.test fail\"]\n  mm --\u003e fail2[\"per-rule exclude miss\"]\n  cov --\u003e fail3[\"coverage gate false green\"]\n```\n\n## 1. Package scripts — drop Unix shell syntax\n\nFile: [package.json](package.json)\n\n| Current | Problem | Fix |\n|---------|---------|-----|\n| `\"remove-buildinfo\": \"rm -rf …\"` | Needs Bun shell / fails under cmd | Tiny Bun one-liner: `bun -e \"try{await Bun.file('tsconfig.types.tsbuildinfo').unlink()}catch{}\"` (or delete via `node:fs`). Drop the odd `postbuild` → `--shell bun remove-buildinfo` indirection; call the unlink script directly from `postbuild`. |\n| `\"test:coverage\": \"AGENT=1 bun run …\"` | POSIX env prefix; breaks PowerShell/cmd | Set `AGENT: \"1\"` inside [scripts/coverage-threshold.ts](scripts/coverage-threshold.ts) spawn `env` (script already spreads `process.env`). Script becomes `\"bun run scripts/coverage-threshold.ts\"`. |\n\nKeep `\u0026\u0026` chains — they work under `bun run`. Document that scripts are meant to be invoked via Bun, not raw npm/cmd.\n\n## 2. Path utilities — normalize before match/split\n\nAdd a small helper (e.g. in [src/config.ts](src/config.ts) or a tiny `src/paths.ts`):\n\n```ts\nexport function toPosixPath(p: string): string {\n  return p.replaceAll(\"\\\\\", \"/\");\n}\n```\n\nUse it consistently:\n\n- [src/index.ts](src/index.ts) `isSelfPath`: split on `/` **after** `toPosixPath`, or use `path.parse` / segment walk that accepts both seps.\n- [src/config.ts](src/config.ts) `isFileExcludedForRule`: `minimatch(toPosixPath(relPath), pattern, …)` so Windows `relPath` matches config patterns written with `/`.\n- [src/index.ts](src/index.ts) / [src/cli.ts](src/cli.ts) / [src/rules/runner.ts](src/rules/runner.ts): when emitting relative paths for display/JSON/dedup keys, normalize with `toPosixPath(path.relative(...))` so output is stable across OSes.\n- [src/rules/all-rules.test.ts](src/rules/all-rules.test.ts): replace `file.split(\"/\").at(-1)` with `path.basename(file)`.\n\nConfig docs keep forward-slash globs (`\"src/generated/**\"`) — that is the portable convention; code adapts paths to match.\n\n## 3. CLI entry guard\n\n[src/cli.ts](src/cli.ts) line 40:\n\n```ts\nif (import.meta.url === `file://${process.argv[1]}`) {\n```\n\nReplace with Bun’s portable check: `if (import.meta.main) { … }`. Keep `#!/usr/bin/env bun` (harmless on Windows; required for Unix direct exec).\n\n## 4. Coverage threshold regex\n\n[scripts/coverage-threshold.ts](scripts/coverage-threshold.ts) line 34 only matches `src/…`. Change to accept either separator:\n\n```ts\n/^\\s+(src[/\\\\]\\S+)\\s+\\|\\s+([\\d.]+)\\s+\\|/\n```\n\nOptionally normalize the captured path with `toPosixPath` in failure messages.\n\n## 5. Tests that hardcode `/`\n\n- [src/dedup.test.ts](src/dedup.test.ts): build abs path with `path.join(process.cwd(), \"src\", \"foo.ts\")`; expect `\"src/foo.ts\"` (posix-normalized output from step 2).\n- [src/config.test.ts](src/config.test.ts): build exclude patterns with `path.join` / `toPosixPath` so the e2e exclude matches Windows `relPath`.\n- [src/index.test.ts](src/index.test.ts): add a backslash-path case for `shouldProcessFile(\"some\\\\rule-validator\\\\file.ts\", …)`.\n\n## 6. <think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
The three simplify agents returned clear findings.

Seven fixes are planned. A `toRelativePosix` helper will be added to paths.ts and used across index.ts, runner.ts, cli.ts, and config.test.ts. Coverage-threshold imports will switch to `toPosixPath`. `checkLineForViolations` will compute `relPath` once inside `scanFile`. The AST will emit relative POSIX paths at the runner boundary for JSON deduplication. A narrating comment in paths.ts will be removed. The custom-hooks quality check flags fragility; it will remain unchanged since `bunx` requires a dist build.

A more robust `custom-hooks` approach is being considered. A small script using `require.resolve` or `import.meta.resolve` could resolve the package before running the CLI, avoiding the fragility of direct `bun` commands.

The package name mismatched the installed name, so `import.meta.resolve` was dismissed. A hardcoded relative path was also rejected. `createRequire` is now the preferred approach.

The `createRequire` script will locate the package root by resolving `stepdown-rule/package.json`, then join `src/cli.ts` to run the CLI. This avoids hardcoded paths and handles hoisting. Double `toPosixPath` normalization in `isFileExcludedForRule` is harmless because it is idempotent.

`scanFile` will pre-filter excluded rules into `fileSkippedRules` and compute `relPath` once at the start. This avoids repeated recomputation during line scanning.

Moving path-based exclusion into `scanFile` would let `checkLineForViolations` drop its path parameter entirely. But the function is exported and tested, so shifting that logic risks breaking existing tests that pass `ruleExcludes` directly. The test usage needs review first.

</details></think>

| File:line                | Code                                                     |
| ------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------- |
| `src/index.ts:53`        | `toPosixPath(path.relative(process.cwd(), file))`        |
| `src/index.ts:118`       | `toPosixPath(path.relative(process.cwd(), filePath))`    |

| `src/config.test.ts:105` | `toPosixPath(path.relative(process.cwd(), fixturePath))` |
| `src/config.test.ts:118` | `toPosixPath(path.relative(process.cwd(), srcDir))`      |

**Suggested reuse** in `src/paths.ts`:

```ts
export function toRelativePosix(file: string, cwd = process.cwd()): string {
	return toPosixPath(path.relative(cwd, file));
}
```

Replace all five call sites. This is the main reuse miss.

---

### FIX — `cli.ts` absolute-aware variant belongs in same helper

`src/cli.ts:101-103`:

```ts
toPosixPath(path.isAbsolute(v.file) ? path.relative(process.cwd(), v.file) : v.file);
```

Same intent as above; only difference is skipping `relative` when already relative. Prefer one helper that covers both:

```ts
export function toRelativePosix(file: string, cwd = process.cwd()): string {
	const rel = path.isAbsolute(file) ? path.relative(cwd, file) : file;
	return toPosixPath(rel);
}
```

Then production sites that always `path.relative(...)` can still call it (absolute inputs from glob/TS are fine; relative inputs stay relative). **Fix.**

```

// ...

```

Regex at `:34` (`src[/\\]`) stays — that's matching, not normalizing. **Fix the replace only.**

## Verdict

One real hot-path bug: regex scan normalizes/excludes **per line**. AST path is fine. Scripts are not perf issues.

### Worth fixing now

**1. `checkLineForViolations` — `path.relative` + `toPosixPath` every line**
`src/index.ts:116-121` (called from `scanFile` `:105-112`)

File path never changes across lines, yet each line does:

```118:121:src/index.ts
	const relPath = toPosixPath(path.relative(process.cwd(), filePath));
	for (const rule of RULES) {
		if (fileSkippedRules?.has(rule.name)) continue;
		if (isFileExcludedForRule(relPath, rule.name, ruleExcludes)) continue;
```

Cost ≈ `files × lines × (relative + replace)`. Exclude matching is also **file-scoped** but re-run every rule×line.

**Fix:** compute `relPath` once in `scanFile`; fold config excludes into the same `fileSkippedRules` Set (or a sibling set) before the line loop. Pass that into `checkLineForViolations` — no path work on the line hot path.

Callers already pass posix `relPath` (`index.ts:118`, `runner.ts:35`). Pattern normalize every call is tiny; better normalize patterns once at config load. **Skip unless touching #1.**

**3. `runRules` per-file relative** — `src/rules/runner.ts:34-37`

**4. `createAnalyzer` normalize** — `src/typescript/compiler.ts:60-74`
Once at setup; needed so glob paths match TS `file.fileName` on Windows. **Keep. Not duplicated work.**

**coverage-threshold inline `replaceAll`** — `scripts/coverage-threshold.ts:37`

## Recommended type model (minimal)

```typescript
/** OS-native path for fs.readFile / glob yields */
type FsPath = string & { readonly __brand: unique symbol };

/** Project-root-relative, forward-slash only — for output, JSON, minimatch */
type RelativePosixPath = string & { readonly __brand: unique symbol };

export function toRelativePosix(file: FsPath, cwd?: string): RelativePosixPath;
export function toPosixPath(p: string): RelativePosixPath; // when input already relative
```

Then thread `RelativePosixPath` through `DisplayViolation`, `JsonViolation`, `RuleResult`, and `isFileExcludedForRule` — drop defensive double-normalize or keep as idempotent safety inside one function.
